I469.screening_reason: Population not specified as students; no method or results reported
I469.summary_en: Aims to classify whether people are currently suffering from stress using questionnaire responses and machine learning algorithms. The abstract mainly discusses ethical considerations and does not specify the population, algorithms or results.

I470.best_result: Autoencoder F1 improvement of 5% (PHQ-9) and 6% (SAS) over prior studies
I470.summary_en: Monitors depression and anxiety in 176 quarantined college students during COVID-19 using multidimensional smartphone data (GPS, phone activity) collected via an Android app, with PHQ-9 and SAS as labels. An autoencoder model improves F1 by 5% (PHQ-9) and 6% (SAS) relative to existing studies.

I471.summary_en: Designs an AI-based psychological health service system for college students, identifying user demand indexes through questionnaires, interviews and the analytic hierarchy process (AHP). Proposes a framework built around an AI cloud platform for long-term monitoring and prediction, without reporting evaluation results.

I472.summary_en: Classifies student stress levels (low, moderate, high) from academic and personal variables using SVM, Decision Trees, ANN and AdaBoost. Decision Tree achieves high accuracy; study hours, sleep duration and GPA are the most influential predictors.

I473.summary_en: Predicts nomophobia (fear of being without a mobile phone) using Naive Bayes, KNN, MLP and SVM with random-search tuning and k-fold cross-validation. SVM outperforms the other models; the data and population are not described.

I474.screening_reason: Main focus is in-class behaviour and engagement; well-being is secondary
I474.summary_en: Analyses students' class lecture activity in Bangladesh using MotionWatch 8 actigraphy and a questionnaire to predict student behaviour, emotional state and attention with ensemble, deep learning and machine learning models. A hybrid model performs best, and SHAP, LIME and permutation importance are used for interpretability.

I475.summary_en: Classifies physical, social and cognitive stressors from ECG-derived heart rate variability features recorded with a Hexoskin smart shirt in 26 college students, as a step towards anxiety prediction. An SVM achieves 76.2% binary and 79.1% multi-class accuracy.

I476.summary_en: Develops an AI-powered chatbot based on cognitive behavioural therapy techniques to support stress and anxiety in university students, evaluated with 47 Peruvian students aged 19-26. It obtains a mean System Usability Scale score of 82.13 and promising reductions in GAD-7 and PSS-14 scores.

I477.screening_reason: Population: higher education teachers, not students
I477.summary_en: Proposes a multilayer Bi-LSTM with attention to predict psychological stress in higher education faculty from physiological, behavioural and environmental data on benchmark datasets. It achieves 94.27% accuracy and AUC 0.972, outperforming SVM, Random Forest and LSTM.

I478.screening_reason: Main focus is personalised learning; emotional well-being is secondary
I478.summary_en: Proposes FocusED, a personalised learning framework for neurodivergent students combining NLP, multimodal behavioural modelling and affect-aware adaptation that detects emotional states and provides supportive interventions. Using learner interaction logs, it achieves 96.51% learning outcome prediction accuracy and reports improved emotional stability.

I479.summary_en: Investigates the feasibility of classifying students' anxiety and depression from the content of their Facebook posts using machine learning. The abstract does not describe the dataset size, algorithms or results.

I480.best_result: Fine-tuned BERT accuracy 98.91% (mental health classification); RF accuracy 83.66% (emotion recognition)
I480.summary_en: Presents a dual-modality system combining speech emotion recognition (eight emotions) with NLP-based classification of students' mental health concerns into academic, non-academic or mixed categories. Random Forest reaches 83.66% for emotion recognition and fine-tuned BERT 98.91% for text classification, with LIME and SHAP explanations.

I481.best_result: Accuracy above 93% for all trained models
I481.summary_en: Develops the Depression Possibility Detection Tool for Sri Lankan undergraduates using facial expressions, eye movements, behavioural changes (step count, phone usage) and physical conditions (heart rate, sleep). CNN (VGG16), ResNet-50 and Random Forest models each exceed 93% accuracy.

I482.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; data and method not clearly described
I482.summary_en: Proposes a machine learning-based physical education analytics framework (MPEA-CI) to assess the impact of physical education programmes on students' emotional well-being. The abstract does not describe the data or model and reports only that it outperforms existing techniques by 95.21%.

I483.summary_en: Detects stress and academic risk among higher education students affected by social media, using TF-IDF features and a Fuzzy SVM on three benchmark datasets. Fuzzy SVM reaches 95.27% accuracy and 95.69% F1, outperforming traditional SVM.

I484.screening_reason: Population: children and adolescents, not explicitly students
I484.summary_en: Compares eight machine learning algorithms (SVM variants, KNN, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Logistic Regression) for detecting depressive symptoms in children and adolescents. Linear SVM is the most accurate (95.54%); the data are not described.

I485.screening_reason: Not about mental health or students; social work information system
I485.summary_en: Designs a social work system based on computer big data and ecosystem theory using UML. It reports good application results without addressing student mental health.

I486.summary_en: Compares CNN, RNN, LSTM and Bi-LSTM on Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale survey data (demographic, psychometric and academic variables) from higher education students in Oman. Bi-LSTM achieves the highest accuracy in identifying students with mental health issues.

I487.summary_en: Proposes a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network with z-score normalisation and SVR-based feature selection to detect social media addiction among students. It reports 95.62% accuracy; the dataset is not described.

I488.summary_en: Designs a psychological test process and system for university students based on the Apriori association rule algorithm to identify common mental health problems. No evaluation results are reported.

I489.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep pattern, not mental health directly
I489.summary_en: Classifies regular versus irregular sleep patterns in 286 university students from an online survey of demographics, daily habits and perceptions using Random Forest with 5-fold cross-validation. It achieves 81.46% mean accuracy; sleep hours, late-night frequency, sleep quality, fatigue and illness frequency are the most influential features.

I490.screening_reason: Outcome is mental health literacy; population includes multiple institutional stakeholder groups
I490.summary_en: Designs a user-centred dashboard to visualise heterogeneity in mental health literacy across stakeholder groups in an educational institution, based on profiles derived by latent profile analysis. Mental health professionals rated the prototype as useful, intuitive and easy to navigate.

I491.summary_en: Introduces CanChat, a Cantonese empathetic chatbot to support secondary school students in Hong Kong with academic and family challenges, provide mental health information and alert social workers when needed. No data, model details or evaluation results are reported.

I492.summary_en: Analyses PISA 2018 data to identify factors associated with happiness among East Asian students and its relationship with reading, mathematics and science achievement. Frequency of being happy, subjective well-being and frequency of being joyful show the strongest positive correlations with happiness (r > 0.4).

I493.summary_en: Proposes a system to predict student anxiety from images, videos and text, using CNN, VGG16, AlexNet and GoogLeNet for emotional cues in visual data and TF-IDF with XGBoost for text. No evaluation results are reported.

I494.screening_reason: Population: university-affiliated military members, not clearly students
I494.summary_en: Proposes a passive smartwatch-based monitoring framework with a deep neural network fusing multimodal physiological signals to detect precursors of stress, validated on a cohort of university-affiliated military members. It reports effectiveness in tracking perceived stress without quantitative metrics.

I495.screening_reason: General review, not specific to students
I495.summary_en: Reviews previous studies on artificial intelligence and machine learning for early detection of mental stress and other mental health issues across students and professionals. The abstract does not describe the review method or specific findings.

I496.screening_reason: Outcome is school dropout, not mental health
I496.summary_en: Applies a machine learning-based methodology to real-world data on students who dropped out to identify causes of attrition across schools and support regional monitoring. No model details or results are reported.

I497.summary_en: Predicts anxiety levels in university students using K-NN, Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression on questionnaire data including demographics, CGPA, scholarship and anxiety symptoms. The models are to be evaluated and no results are reported.

I498.screening_reason: Not about mental health or students; teacher education culture
I498.summary_en: Proposes an Internet+ model algorithm to construct a college teacher education culture system and states that its feasibility was confirmed by testing. It does not address student mental health.

I499.screening_reason: Outcome is higher education quality evaluation, not mental health
I499.summary_en: Proposes EduTabNet-AE, combining TabNet with attention and ensemble learning to evaluate higher education quality on benchmark educational datasets. It achieves 96.8% accuracy and 96.5% F1 with explainable attention.

I500.summary_en: Proposes an AI-enhanced mental health tool to provide students with real-time, personalised support for academic stress, motivated by student suicide statistics in India. No data, method or evaluation results are described.

I501.best_result: Up to 97% accuracy in reviewed studies
I501.summary_en: Systematic literature review following PRISMA of 20 studies (2019-2025) on machine learning prediction of student stress and academic performance. Random Forest, SVM and neural networks are the most frequent algorithms, with accuracies up to 97%, and explainable AI and multimodal integration are identified as future needs.

I502.screening_reason: Population includes students and working professionals; focus on productivity
I502.summary_en: Presents Eunoia, a web-based virtual assistant combining mood tracking based on Russell's circumplex model, a Random Forest regressor for task urgency and a TF-IDF/TextBlob sentiment chatbot for students and working professionals. User testing with 60 participants showed strong usability and positive emotional impact.

I503.summary_en: Classifies suicidal behaviours in medical students from an expert-developed self-report questionnaire (688 instances, 342 features on socioeconomic status, substance use and trauma) using SVM and Random Forest. SVM achieves AUC 0.81 and Random Forest 0.80.

I504.screening_reason: Outcome is learning disabilities, not mental health
I504.summary_en: Proposes a machine learning framework for early detection of learning disabilities in primary school students using academic records, behavioural observations and cognitive test results. It reports promising accuracy, precision and recall without specific values.

I505.screening_reason: Not about mental health; intelligent homework system
I505.summary_en: Proposes an intelligent homework system based on big data and an adaptive learning model to address challenges in post-pandemic online education. It does not address mental health.

I506.summary_en: Proposes a student mental health monitoring model fusing hard data (speech emotion recognition with CNN-LSTM to estimate depression probability) and soft data (psychologists' opinions modelled with Dempster-Shafer theory). No dataset or evaluation results are reported.

I507.summary_en: Predicts four stages of depression and anxiety in university students in Bangladesh from text input using Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, neural networks, KNN and a stacking model with LDA as meta-classifier, trained on over 10,800 (depression) and 14,500 (anxiety) records. The stacking model achieves 99% and 97% test accuracy.

I508.summary_en: Detects stress levels in students with social media addiction using preprocessed social media content, mRMR and chi-square feature selection, and an attention-based graph convolutional network. The model achieves 92.84% accuracy, outperforming Random Forest and standard GCN.

I509.screening_reason: Population: electronics engineers, not clearly students
I509.summary_en: Investigates digital dependency among 268 electronics engineering participants using exploratory factor analysis, a supervised pipeline predicting moderate or severe dependency and K-Means clustering yielding five usage personas. Sleep disruption, reduced academic satisfaction and anxiety-mediated impulsivity dominate the dependency profile.

I510.summary_en: Examines, through a literature review and case studies, the relationship between IoT-sensed workplace environmental data, sedentary behaviour and job satisfaction among academic staff. No original analysis or results are reported.

I511.summary_en: Compares machine learning classifiers for detecting the psychological impact of COVID-19 on Malaysian postgraduate students using an online survey dataset from Mendeley (GAD-7 and concerns about research progress, academic delay and daily life). An artificial neural network achieves the highest accuracy (95.45%), with Logistic Regression, linear SVM and Gaussian Process above 90%.

I512.screening_reason: Focus is learning support for dyslexia; mental health only mentioned as a consequence
I512.summary_en: Describes VRAIlexia, a framework combining artificial intelligence and virtual reality to provide personalised digital tools and learning strategies for university students with dyslexia. No data, model or evaluation results are reported.

I513.screening_reason: Conference front matter; not a study
I513.summary_en: General co-chairs' welcome message for the 8th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA 2022). It contains no study.

I514.best_result: Optimised Logistic Regression and XGBoost (best recall-accuracy trade-off)
I514.summary_en: Predicts suicidal ideation in university students from psychological and demographic data using Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, neural networks and XGBoost with RFECV feature selection and class balancing. Optimised Logistic Regression and XGBoost give the best balance of recall and accuracy; depression, hopelessness, loneliness and neurodivergence diagnosis are key predictors.

I515.screening_reason: Focus is the impact of smoking on academic life
I515.summary_en: Examines the impact of smoking on graduate students' academic life using several machine learning algorithms on a collected dataset. KNN and Random Forest both reach 87.93% accuracy; students who smoke tended to have poorer academic results.

I516.screening_reason: Outcome is opinions on COVID-19 vaccination, not mental health
I516.summary_en: Assesses college students' opinions about the COVID-19 vaccine through social network and sentiment analysis with Naive Bayes, SVM and Logistic Regression. The abstract does not describe the dataset or results.

I517.screening_reason: Bibliometric analysis of ADHD adolescent behaviour research; not students' mental health analytics
I517.summary_en: Applies CiteSpace knowledge mapping to the literature on adolescent ADHD behaviour research, analysing publication stages, disciplines, collaboration networks and keywords. The field shows interdisciplinary expansion, international collaboration, refinement and extension.

I518.summary_en: Evaluates student academic performance from internal and external factors, including mental health issues, using the Student Performance Dataset 2024 (98,000 samples, 41 features) and five classifiers. Decision Tree reaches 99.999% cross-validation and 100% hold-out accuracy, and LIME identifies the top five predictors.

I519.screening_reason: Outcome is physical health status, not mental health
I519.summary_en: Develops an automatic sports results recording and health promotion system for college students that uses wearable physiological data and an SVM to classify health risk levels. Simulation experiments report high accuracy and reliability without specific values.

I520.best_result: Random Forest + XGBoost Voting Classifier accuracy 80.28%, weighted F1 0.81
I520.summary_en: Predicts student stress levels (low, moderate, high) from 243 survey responses with 31 attributes using a Voting Classifier combining Random Forest and XGBoost, benchmarked against KNN and Naive Bayes. The ensemble achieves 80.28% accuracy and a weighted F1 of 0.81.

I521.best_result: Random Forest with Word2Vec accuracy 99%, F1 94%
I521.summary_en: Detects mental stress in university students from online forum text posts using Word2Vec features and Random Forest. The model achieves 99% accuracy and 94% F1, outperforming Naive Bayes, KNN, Decision Tree and SVM.

I522.screening_reason: Outcome is classroom engagement, not mental health
I522.summary_en: Classifies student engagement in the classroom from images using transfer learning with a CNN and MobileNet on a small custom dataset. The model achieves 93% overall accuracy.

I523.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance; no mental health component
I523.summary_en: Predicts student academic performance from survey-based smartphone usage patterns using several classifiers. Logistic Regression achieves the highest accuracy, and usage patterns are significantly correlated with performance.

I524.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance (GPA); no mental health component
I524.summary_en: Examines the effect of credit load on semester GPA of computer science students at a Sri Lankan university using decision trees, Random Forest and SVM. It finds a weak correlation between credit load and academic performance.

I525.summary_en: Proposes a neuro-symbolic framework combining a neural network with rule-based reasoning on academic, behavioural, social and psychological factors to predict student stress. It achieves 93% accuracy, and SHAP and rule-based insights explain stress-related features; the dataset is not described.

I526.summary_en: Presents EMO-Music, a smartwatch-based system that recognises users' emotions from physiological signals with deep learning and plays music accordingly to support college students' well-being. Feasibility was evaluated with the SUS scale, but no results are reported.

I527.best_result: Linear Regression stress MAE 1.242, R2 0.008; sleep MAE 1.416, R2 0.112
I527.summary_en: Predicts daily stress and sleep quality from passive smartphone sensing in the StudentLife dataset (48 Dartmouth undergraduates over 10 weeks) using Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and MLP with leave-one-subject-out validation. Linear Regression is competitive and complex models give no consistent advantage; SHAP identifies physical activity ratio and conversation duration as the main stress predictors.

I528.summary_en: Examines, with structural equation modelling on questionnaire data, how the parent-child relationship relates to smartphone reliance, academic procrastination and self-esteem in 475 grade-nine students in Changzhou. A poorer parent-child relationship is associated with greater smartphone reliance and procrastination, while a better one supports self-esteem.

I529.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; not about mental health
I529.summary_en: Discusses a distributed Internet architecture for multi-agent systems and the development of college physical education teaching with information technology. It does not address mental health.

I530.best_result: Training time reduced by 11.2%, 43.3% and 39.1% versus baselines
I530.summary_en: Proposes mining college students' psychological and behavioural patterns by combining genetic algorithm feature selection with a deep neural network optimised by differential evolution. The model reduces training time by 11.2%, 43.3% and 39.1% compared with baselines; the data are not described.

I531.screening_reason: General literature review, not specific to students
I531.summary_en: Reviews literature on data mining techniques for diagnosing depression and anxiety, retrieving 29 papers of which 17 were identified as significant works. It concludes that data mining can substantially support diagnosis prediction.

I532.best_result: Random Forest and KNN accuracy up to 85%
I532.summary_en: Models a person's likely mental state (depression, anxiety, OCD, insomnia) from music preferences, comparing five models. Random Forest and KNN reach up to 85% accuracy; exploratory analysis links high depression, OCD and insomnia to Lofi and higher anxiety to Folk and K-pop.

I533.summary_en: Classifies student depression from real-world survey data on behavioural, academic and lifestyle factors using resampling and boosting algorithms (Gradient Boosting, XGBoost). All models exceed 90% accuracy with XGBoost best, and SHAP highlights gender, age, academic pressure, CGPA and study satisfaction.

I534.screening_reason: Population: adults over 18 assessed by a French university, not explicitly students
I534.summary_en: Detects anxiety, depression and panic attacks from numerical responses of 4,184 people over 18 diagnosed by a French university, using SMOTE and a stacking ensemble of Random Forest, SVM, KNN and AdaBoost. The stacking ensemble achieves the highest accuracy compared with individual classifiers.

I535.best_result: XGBoost with HRM + SBERT features F1 0.86, recall 93%
I535.summary_en: Proposes an explainable user-level framework combining human-readable behavioural metrics with Sentence-BERT embeddings and an XGBoost classifier on the University of Maryland Reddit Suicidality Dataset. It achieves F1 up to 0.86 and 93% recall for at-risk users, with SHAP explanations.

I536.screening_reason: Outcome is student failure and dropout, not mental health
I536.best_result: EduBoost 9-11% gains in accuracy, precision, recall and F1 over White-Box baseline (OULAD)
I536.summary_en: Proposes EduBoost, an interpretable grey-box approach combining a voting ensemble of black-box models with a CART white-box model to identify students at risk of failure and dropout, tested on a university course dataset and OULAD. It improves metrics by 9-11% on OULAD and 2-3% on the university dataset over the white-box baseline.

I537.screening_reason: Main outcome is academic performance; alcohol consumption as predictor
I537.summary_en: Analyses how alcohol consumption affects final grades of high school students using public data from Portugal with Python and SAS Viya. Higher drinking is associated with lower grades, while study time and health are associated with better grades; model R2 is modest.

I538.summary_en: Classifies stress levels in undergraduate students from EEG data, comparing raw preprocessed and PCA-reduced features with KNN, Naive Bayes and MLP. KNN achieves the highest mean accuracy (99%), versus about 50% for Naive Bayes and 80% for MLP.

I539.summary_en: Predicts anxiety and depression in people who play games using survey data mainly from students plus some working professionals and several machine learning models. KNN achieves the highest accuracy.

I540.summary_en: Models job burnout among college teachers with a multilayer perceptron on the Kaggle 'Are Your Employees Burning Out?' dataset. The model reaches 0.98 accuracy and 0.965 F1.

I541.summary_en: Predicts stress levels in 2,028 Bangladeshi university students from PSS-10 items selected with PCA and information gain, using Logistic Regression tuned by Artificial Bee Colony optimisation. It achieves 98.99% accuracy and 99.01% F1, and LIME shows stress frequency, coping difficulty and perceived loss of control as main drivers.

I542.summary_en: Predicts daily depression scores from longitudinal mobile sensing data of college students over three academic years, using interpolated weekly PHQ-4 labels and a sensor-aware missing-value preprocessing pipeline with regression models. The sensor-aware approach improves performance over standard preprocessing, without reported metrics.

I543.summary_en: Classifies multi-level stress in university students (grouped by PSS-10) from EEG signals segmented into 1-5 second intervals with eight time and frequency features and a Bagged Trees classifier. It reports potential for non-invasive stress monitoring without quantitative results.

I544.summary_en: Develops a cloud-based IoMT system to predict anxiety levels and stages from GAD-7, PHQ-9 and UCLA-8 survey data with demographic factors submitted via a mobile app, comparing several machine learning algorithms. Logistic Regression and LDA achieve 97% accuracy, SVM 95% and CatBoost 94%.

I545.summary_en: Presents SymptoBot, an AI diagnostic website for students of the Polytechnic University of the Philippines integrating PHQ-9 depression screening and an AI chatbot providing psychological first aid. Experimental interactions confirmed accurate and natural responses, without quantitative results.

I546.best_result: Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting and Logistic Regression (near-perfect performance with selected sensor combinations)
I546.summary_en: Explores privacy-preserving depression detection using only non-PII smartphone sensor data from the StudentLife dataset (48 students, 65 days) with prevailing machine learning models. Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting and Logistic Regression perform best, and combinations such as surrounding conversation and phone lock frequency yield near-perfect performance.

I547.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; main focus is AI and robotics in higher education
I547.summary_en: Discusses the role of AI and robotics in higher education and examines factors associated with mental health issues among 210 undergraduate students from Delhi NCR and abroad after COVID-19 using SVM, Naive Bayes and Random Forest with 5-fold cross-validation. The abstract is incoherent and reports no quantitative results.

I548.summary_en: Detects stress levels in undergraduate students (aged 17-23) of Indian technical institutions from PPG-derived heart rate data collected with a Polar OH1+ armband. A classification model on the extracted features achieves over 86% accuracy.

I549.summary_en: Classifies student stress into three categories from 24 features gathered from various studies and data sources, including PHQ-9, using chi-squared SelectKBest feature selection and eight supervised algorithms. SVM achieves the highest accuracy (87.3%), and most students fall into mild stress.

I550.best_result: Stacking (SVM, RF, GB with XGBoost meta-classifier) accuracy 91.16%, ROC-AUC 96.60
I550.summary_en: Proposes a stacking ensemble with SVM, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting as base estimators and XGBoost as final classifier for depression detection in college students, using stratified k-fold cross-validation on a balanced dataset. It achieves 91.16% accuracy, 0.913 F1 and 96.60 ROC-AUC; the dataset is not described.

I551.screening_reason: Not about mental health; golf teaching curriculum
I551.summary_en: Introduces the use of cloud computing and speech recognition for golf teaching and curriculum design in undergraduate colleges. It reports a 7.6% increase in guidance efficiency.

I552.best_result: SVM and Random Forest best on dataset 1; Decision Tree best on dataset 2
I552.summary_en: Predicts depression and mental illness using Random Forest, Decision Tree, SVM, KNN and Naive Bayes with SMOTE and grid search on a Kaggle dataset and a survey collected at six Indian universities. SVM and Random Forest perform best on the first dataset and Decision Tree on the second.

I553.screening_reason: Focus is network architecture; mental health outcomes are not modelled
I553.summary_en: Proposes a standardised 6G edge-cloud IoT framework with federated learning for continuous environmental perception and mental health monitoring on university campuses. Benchmarking shows advantages in latency, energy efficiency, scalability and privacy over cloud-only and edge-only designs, without mental health results.

I554.screening_reason: Main focus is academic performance and personality recommendation
I554.summary_en: Proposes a recommender system that uses polarity-based sentiment analysis and association rule mining on closed-ended questionnaires (emotional intelligence, personality, self-esteem, PANAS, Oxford Happiness) to predict student personality with emotions. No evaluation results are reported.

I555.screening_reason: Population: social media users, not students
I555.summary_en: Classifies depression-related social media posts and comments from about 6,500 entries (including Facebook) annotated by undergraduate students, using TF-IDF features and eight classifiers. Gradient Boosting performs best with about 98.5% accuracy.

I556.summary_en: Develops a face recognition application based on deep neural networks for teacher well-being self-assessment using the Neuroresearch method. No quantitative results are reported.

I557.screening_reason: No explicit data analytics or machine learning method described
I557.summary_en: Reviews prior work on analysing students' behavioural patterns and learning curves during COVID-19 to identify psychologically disturbed students. The abstract does not describe the review method or findings.

I558.best_result: Voice stress detection accuracy 90% (anxiety); chatbot accuracy 85%
I558.summary_en: Presents EQU ACCESS, an online education approach combining behavioural expression analysis, an emotional support chatbot, voice stress detection and visual content description to support students' emotional well-being. It reports 90% accuracy for voice-based anxiety detection, 85% for the chatbot and a 30% rise in perceived emotional support; the data are not described.

I559.summary_en: Estimates depression in 820 university students by fusing behavioural (mobility, smartphone use, sleep) and linguistic features (essays, social media posts) with PHQ-9 labels, comparing BERT, RoBERTa, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and a fusion ensemble. The fusion ensemble outperforms unimodal baselines with 86% accuracy, and SHAP identifies the most influential predictors.

I560.screening_reason: Population: AUD patients and controls, not students
I560.summary_en: Detects alcohol use disorder from EEG effective connectivity (DTF and PDC) in 30 patients and 30 healthy controls using a machine learning model. PDC features achieve higher accuracy (94.5%) than DTF (89.8%).

I561.summary_en: Proposes a digital twin platform for stress management in higher education integrating wearable physiological data (heart rate, HRV, activity, sleep), self-reports and academic context with machine learning to predict individual stress and personalise interventions. Initial results suggest that combining biosignals with academic data improves stress prediction, without reported metrics.

I562.summary_en: Reviews applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning for detecting and preventing social media addiction and related mental distress among students aged 12 to 18. The abstract does not describe the review method or number of studies.

I563.best_result: Gradient Boosting accuracy 83.8% (anxiety, depression); Random Forest 77.3% (stress)
I563.summary_en: Classifies five severity levels of anxiety, depression and stress in university students from personal information and mental health survey responses using Gradient Boosting, Random Forest and KNN stacking with rebalancing. Gradient Boosting reaches 83.8% accuracy for anxiety and depression and Random Forest 77.3% for stress.

I564.screening_reason: Not data analytics or machine learning; review of stigma interventions
I564.summary_en: Reviews 8-10 papers on causes of mental illness stigma in healthcare settings and strategies to reduce it. RESHAPE, KAP and IBH interventions are reported as effective.

I565.best_result: Instance-based methods accuracy gain over 14 percentage points with interaction features
I565.summary_en: Tests whether interaction features built from study hours, sleep, social media use and mental health status improve academic performance prediction on a simulated dataset of 1,000 students with nine Weka classifiers. Interaction terms raise instance-based model accuracy by over 14 percentage points and modestly improve ensembles.

I566.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance; no mental health component
I566.summary_en: Compares ten supervised algorithms for predicting student pass/fail and multi-class academic performance. Logistic Regression achieves 93.4% in the binary case, while ensemble and boosting models perform well in the multi-class setup.

I567.summary_en: Examines the relationship between gameplay log data from custom shooter and memory games and depression and anxiety in 56 university students using correlation, linear regression, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, ANOVA and Mann-Whitney U tests. Several in-game behaviours, log size, tutorial skipping, age and help-seeking are significantly related to depression and anxiety.

I568.screening_reason: Not about mental health analytics; institutional digital transformation
I568.summary_en: Reflection paper describing the campusX digital transformation initiative at the Singapore University of Technology and Design for cyber-physical learning. It does not analyse mental health data.

I569.screening_reason: Population: Facebook users, not explicitly students; outcome includes academic performance
I569.summary_en: Analyses Facebook addiction and its effects on academic work from a Google Forms survey of 2,222 Bangladeshi Facebook users, testing several machine learning models. Gradient Boosting achieves the best prediction (94.5%), and higher usage is associated with addictive behaviour and reduced academic concentration.

I570.best_result: Stacking ensemble (SVM, KNN, LR with neural network meta-model) accuracy 96.36%
I570.summary_en: Predicts depression from a Google survey of 550 university students using Logistic Regression, SVM, KNN, Decision Tree and neural networks. The neural network reaches 94.55%, and a stacking ensemble with a neural network meta-model achieves 96.36% accuracy.

I571.summary_en: Proposes Learnease AI, a Django web tool that identifies student emotions and stress levels from facial images (OpenCV), survey answers and behavioural patterns using machine learning, with a dashboard for personalised feedback. It reports high detection accuracy without specific metrics or data description.

I572.summary_en: Applies unsupervised clustering to academic performance data of over 500 students in mid-sized Illinois high schools to classify them as stable, monitor or critical for early detection of mental and behavioural health issues. Cluster sizes are compared with CDC and NAMI adolescent mental health statistics, but no results are reported.

I573.screening_reason: Outcome is physical health, not mental health
I573.summary_en: Proposes an ant-lion-optimised Bi-LSTM (OP_LSTM) for monitoring students' physical health on Kaggle's Student Physical Health dataset. It achieves 0.97 accuracy and 0.97 F1, outperforming existing approaches.

I574.summary_en: Evaluates seven machine learning and four deep learning models with SMOTE and GridSearchCV for classifying stress levels in a secondary PSS-10 dataset of 2,028 university students. Logistic Regression achieves the highest accuracy (99.75%), followed by SVM (99.50% with SMOTE).

I575.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical education action correction
I575.summary_en: Proposes a Hidden Markov Model-assisted correction system to improve student behaviour in university physical education classes. Simulations report a 98.8% predictive rate and 96.8% efficiency.

I576.summary_en: Classifies college students' anxiety into severity levels with a convolutional neural network. The model achieves 98% accuracy and an MSE of 0.02; the dataset is not described.

I577.best_result: Random Forest accuracy 75.91% (severity classification); Gradient Boosting R2 0.522, MAE 4.04 (score regression)
I577.summary_en: Compares machine learning algorithms for classifying PHQ-9 depression severity and for regressing PHQ-9 scores from non-PHQ psychosocial features in university students. Random Forest performs best in classification (75.91%) and Gradient Boosting in regression (R2 0.522, MAE 4.04).

I578.screening_reason: Mental health is only one of several assessment objectives reviewed
I578.summary_en: Systematic review of 51 studies (2015-2024) on intelligent assessment in education, grouping objectives into competence and knowledge, personality and mental health, and teaching and learning processes. It identifies challenges in data collection, model adaptation, and accuracy and interpretability of results.

I579.screening_reason: Conceptual review; population includes working professionals
I579.summary_en: Reviews literature and proposes a conceptual framework integrating AI with Ayurveda and yoga to provide personalised mental health interventions for students and working professionals based on physiological, psychological and lifestyle data. No empirical data or results are reported.

I580.screening_reason: Population: not students; general emotion text dataset
I580.summary_en: Evaluates the effect of re-categorising ISEAR emotions from seven to five classes on CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM and GRU text classifiers for mental health chatbots. CNN reaches 76.4% with five classes versus 61.1% with seven, and deployment in a chatbot in Ghana obtained 65% satisfaction in cultural sensitivity.

I581.screening_reason: Main outcome is concentration and cognitive state
I581.summary_en: Develops a system that classifies student concentration and mental fatigue from EEG, HRV and GSR signals using signal processing and machine learning models. It reports a validated system without quantitative results.

I582.summary_en: Designs an AI-enhanced university counselling solution with rule-based counsellor-student personality matching and machine learning stress assessment, evaluated with survey data from 98 Sri Lankan university students. Random Forest achieves 95.2% accuracy in stress prediction, with study hours, sleep and physical activity as key features, and 80% of students expressed interest.

I583.summary_en: Pilot study predicting self-esteem levels in 47 university students from behaviour-based questionnaire data using an Extreme Learning Machine with ten-fold cross-validation and different activation functions. The best accuracy is 74.5% with ReLU and 16 hidden neurons.

I584.screening_reason: Outcome is course academic performance, not mental health
I584.summary_en: Predicts at-risk performance in the first programming course (CS1) from admissions records and pre-course survey data using several model families, testing on the Fall 2024 cohort. XGBoost performs best (F2 0.71, 81% of at-risk students identified), and SHAP highlights AP scores, calculus background and GPA.

I585.screening_reason: Outcome is institutional ranking by academic performance, not mental health
I585.summary_en: Proposes FEdRank, a federated learning framework enabling universities to collaboratively train models on academic performance metrics such as CGPA and placements to rank institutions with Borda count. It reports stable convergence and accuracy across institutions without specific values.
